sections.title: 2. Engineering Courses in Ireland
items: Undergraduate engineering degrees in Ireland are offered by Irish institutions in a range of disciplines.
The course you choose should be relevant to your interests and the type of work you wish to undertake.
- Bachelor of Engineering (BE or BEng): generally four years.
Bachelor of Engineering and Master of Engineering (integrated course): Usually five years.
Engineering technology or regular-degree paths: duration and career track differ.

4. Eligibility for Study Engineering in Ireland
items: In Ireland, the engineering eligibility criteria differ depending on the institution, the engineering discipline, and the category of applicant.
Usually required for Undergraduate Engineering applicants:
Successfully passed Class 12 or equivalent secondary-school education. - Evidence of strong academic performance in Mathematics
Physics and other science subjects as required.
Any other subject or grade requirements imposed by the university
Universities assess Indian Class 12 qualifications individually.
Mathematics is especially important for engineering and physics and chemistry requirements vary by program.
Admission requirements for engineering in Ireland generally include
Academic requirements: Normally applicants should have a recognized secondary-school qualification including mathematics and any science subjects required.
English Language Requirements: Universities may accept IELTS Academic, TOEFL, or other approved tests. The minimum scores vary by institution and program.
Personal statement or references if requested.
Certified translations of documents not issued in English language. -
Any further evidence for Foundation or Pathway Programs (if applicable).

faqs.q: Q1. How long does it take to complete an undergraduate engineering degree in Ireland?
faqs.a: Many bachelor's in engineering degrees are 4 years. Integrated Bachelor and Master of Engineering programs are generally five years in duration. The length varies by university and discipline.

faqs.q: Q2. Is it possible for Indian students to pursue engineering in Ireland after Class 12?
faqs.a: Yes. Indian students can apply if they satisfy the university's academic, mathematics, science-subject, English-language and other criteria. Each institution has its own admission policy and evaluates Indian qualifications on its own.

faqs.q: Q3. How much is the tuition fee for UG engineering in Ireland?
faqs.a: For non-EU students, fees can be in the region of €18,000 to €30,000 per year depending on the university and course. For example, the University of Galway will charge €27,640 for a number of engineering programs in 2026/27, while DCU will charge €17,900 for several four-year programs.

faqs.q: Q4. What engineering courses can I study in Ireland?
faqs.a: The most popular ones include civil, mechanical, electrical, electronic, chemical, biomedical, energy and computer engineering. The disciplines offered depend on the institution and the program structure.

faqs.q: Q5. Am I able to work in Ireland after completing my engineering degree?
faqs.a: Graduates may apply for suitable engineering jobs, subject to vacancies available, the requirements of the employer, qualifications and the immigration permission applicable. Having a degree doesn't mean you will get a job or work authorization.
